extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, PTO officials, congressional staff, and policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts evaluative standards and procedural requirements from legislative analysis of a patent-reform bill covering post-grant review, venue, discovery, expert-witness reliability, applicant-quality programs, and related procedural safeguards. Useful for drafting, litigating, or administering patent-challenge and prosecution processes under the proposed statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliability indicator: use independent-of-litigation methodologies
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a theory or technique has been employed independently of litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This factor flushes out methodologies that exist only in litigation expert-witness testimony and are never employed in actual licensing negotiations. It injects honesty into hypothetical-negotiation analyses by forcing experts to use methodologies that would actually have been used in real-world negotiations rather than metrics used only in an expert’s ‘imaginary parallel universe.’

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliability indicator: account for readily available alternative theories
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the expert has accounted for readily available alternative theories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An expert should not ignore precise and objective metrics of value (e.g., market price of noninfringing alternatives; costs of noninfringing substitutes or design-arounds; cost savings produced by the invention). If such evidence exists, the expert must consider it or provide a persuasive reason not to. Ignoring readily available alternatives is a common sign of bias and should be barred by the court's gatekeeping role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court explanation of Daubert determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: District courts and circuit courts must explain their Daubert determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requiring explanation facilitates appellate review of gatekeeping decisions under proposed subsection (c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-grant review types and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Two types of post grant review proceedings: a first-period proceeding in which any invalidity argument can be presented, and a second-period proceeding limited to considering arguments of novelty and nonobviousness based on patents or printed publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First-window petitions must be brought within 9 months after the patent is issued. The second window is open for the life of the patent after the 9-month window lapses or after any first-period proceeding has concluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeal of inter partes reexam and director-initiated reexam
rubrics_metrics.description: The bill repeals the procedures for inter partes reexam (effective 1 year after enactment) and director-initiated reexam.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for reexam filed before the effective date may continue to be considered. Director-initiated reexam is repealed to avoid potential political pressure on PTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural model: oppositional model (burden on petitioner)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use an oppositional model: burden on the petitioner to show a claim is not patentable, rather than requiring PTO to meet a burden each time new information is presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This model is favored by PTO as allowing speedier adjudication and avoiding the interminable delays seen in inter partes reexam where PTO must reassess repeatedly.

rubrics_metrics.name: PGR completion deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Post grant review proceedings are to be completed within one year after institution, with a possible 6-month extension for good cause or in the event of second-window joinder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The adoption of an oppositional system is intended to allow PTO to comply with these deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standing requirement for petitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioners must have a substantial economic interest adverse to the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a relatively low threshold requiring a showing that some substantial economic activity of the petitioner is hindered by the express or implied threat of the patent's monopoly; it gives patentees some control over when they may be forced to defend in a PGR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumptive immunity for early enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Presumptive immunity from post grant review for a patent enforced in court within three months of its issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patents asserted very early likely involve well-developed commercial disputes; delaying resolution via PGR could unjustifiably harm market shares, so early enforcement affords presumptive protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bar on duplicative attacks: DJ plaintiffs
rubrics_metrics.description: A party that has filed a declaratory-judgment action challenging validity is barred from also challenging the patent in a post grant review proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents duplicative litigation in multiple fora.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for defendant to open second-window proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: A defendant in an infringement action who seeks to open a second-window proceeding must do so within 3 months after his answer to the complaint is due.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule avoids pre-filing defensive petitions and balances the right to seek second-period review without encouraging anticipatory filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bar on successive PGRs/reexams by same party
rubrics_metrics.description: A party that has already sought a post grant review proceeding against a patent is barred from subsequently seeking another post grant review or a reexam for the same patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents repeat attacks and limits dilatory tactics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estoppel from PGR proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: A party that brought a post grant review proceeding is estopped from raising in any subsequent PTO or ITC proceeding or civil action any claim against that patent that it did raise in the post grant proceeding or that it could have raised in a second-window proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies could-have-raised estoppel to prevent relitigation of issues; raises policy questions when second-window scope is narrow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privity for estoppel purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Privity is a practical, equitable concept used to determine when estoppel applies to related parties; there is no universally applicable definition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Privity often involves successive interests in the same property, but is limited to the rights transferred; not all contractual relationships imply estoppel privity for section 322 purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidentiary threshold to institute PGR (section 327(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any petition must present evidence that, if unrebutted, would show that a claim in the patent is unpatentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a substantial front-loaded threshold (considerably higher than 'significant new question of patentability') designed to force petitioners to present their best evidence up front and to protect PTO from being overwhelmed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of first-window to resolve important legal questions (section 327(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: First-window proceedings may be used to raise important legal questions early in the life of controversies (e.g., whether a particular subject matter is patentable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsection (b) allows PTO to address and, where appropriate, certify important legal questions for Federal Circuit resolution before widespread issuance of improper patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Successive-petition bar for second-period review (section 327(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applies a successive-petition bar to second or successive petitions for second-period review; such repeat review is allowed only in exceptional circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to ensure second or successive proceedings are rare to avoid lengthy and duplicative proceedings that prevent enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director identification of issues forming basis for grant (encouraged but not mandated)
rubrics_metrics.description: It would be desirable for the Director, when granting petitions, to identify issues he found sufficiently established and those he did not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such practice would expedite proceedings by limiting issues and guiding patent-owners' amendments, but mandating it could create problems if the board's view of the central issue shifts; therefore it is recommended practice, not statutory requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joinder and consolidation rules (section 325)
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple first-period proceedings must be consolidated; multiple second-period proceedings may be joined; additional first-period petitions must be joined with the first one and be 'properly filed.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director has discretion to reject additional first-period petitions that add nothing new; the statute intends to avoid notice-and-comment-style inundation of repetitive petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and requirements of 'properly filed'
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition is 'properly filed' when delivered and accepted in compliance with applicable filing rules; time deadlines for filing must be complied with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This term of art is informed by Artuz v. Bennett, Pace v. DiGuglielmo, and Allen v. Siebert: delivery/acceptance and rule compliance are required even if particular claims may be procedurally barred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director discretion to join untimely petitions if high threshold met
rubrics_metrics.description: If a 329(b)(2) deadline for a joinder motion is missed, the Director may still join an additional second-period petition to a pending proceeding if the petition satisfies section 327(c)’s threshold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages timely joinder motions but preserves Director discretion to join petitions that independently meet the successive-petition standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTO discretion to consolidate, stay, or terminate PTO proceedings (section 325(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: PTO may consolidate, stay, or terminate PTO proceedings involving a patent that is the subject of postgrant review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director may stay a PGR during exhaustion of reexam, or consolidate/terminate other PTO proceedings when a PGR is near completion to avoid duplication and inefficient parallel proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery standards for first-window and second-window (section 329)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 329(a)(5) prescribes discovery standards for first-window proceedings; section 329(b)(3) sets more limited standards for second-period discovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Second-period discovery is limited because issues are narrower and the burden on patent owners is greater; subparagraph (A) allows depositions of witnesses submitting statements, and (B) allows further discovery 'as necessary in the interest of justice' but limited to routine minor discovery or special circumstances. Given tight deadlines, PTO is expected to be conservative in granting discovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation of second-window issues to 102 and 103 based on patents and printed publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Second-period proceedings are limited to novelty (102) and nonobviousness (103) arguments based on patents or printed publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This narrow scope reduces the need for discovery and mitigates burdens on patent owners, but also limits second-window utility for accused infringers who may have other defenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concerns about could-have-raised estoppel in second-window context
rubrics_metrics.description: Applying could-have-raised estoppel to the second window may not protect the interests it is intended to vindicate because the second window's issues are sharply limited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because accused infringers will often still need to litigate other defenses in district court, the goal of flushing out all claims in one forum is unattainable; other statutory restrictions (sections 327 and 322) better protect patent owners from abusive proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Venue reform: activities-based test and 'significant' activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt an activities-based test for venue: some significant activity involving either the patent or the infringing product must take place in the district for venue to be proper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The bill uses 'significant' (construed akin to 'legitimate' and evaluable on the face of the activity) rather than 'substantial' to avoid requiring discovery into the whole of which an activity may be a part, and to limit preliminary venue litigation. Courts and litigants are expected to use common sense and not require merits determinations to decide venue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Venue: research and development treated as unified concept
rubrics_metrics.description: Research and development are treated as a unified concept for venue purposes, rather than separated into distinct categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishing research from development is often impractical; treating them together avoids unnecessary complexity at the venue stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Venue: place of conception and nonprofit-managing-entity venue
rubrics_metrics.description: Venue may be proper where an invention was conceived and where a nonprofit organization that manages inventions for colleges/universities (and the patent) is principally based.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conception can occur in multiple places; an independent contractor managing inventions acts on behalf of the party that retained it, so principal location of such a manager may support venue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interlocutory appeals of claim construction discouraged
rubrics_metrics.description: The bill does not require interlocutory appeals of claim construction to the Federal Circuit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interlocutory appeals risk premature, inadequately-developed record decisions, may waste Federal Circuit resources, and freeze district courts into law-of-the-case constructions that cannot later be changed despite new trial evidence. Claim construction is often a rolling process better decided in the full case context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant quality submissions: voluntary search-and-patentability program
rubrics_metrics.description: PTO should encourage applicants to submit prior-art search reports and patentability analyses, but rather than mandate them, the bill authorizes PTO to offer incentives for voluntary participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandatory requirements raised cost, market, and practical questions (e.g., lack of search-firms meeting PTO specs, unknown private-search costs, and added litigation risk from prosecution statements). A voluntary program with incentives is intended as a trial-run to see what requirements are useful and to reduce low-quality filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: File-wrapper immunity for program participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Prosecution records generated under the PTO search-and-patentability program are inadmissible to construe patent claims in later proceedings (file-wrapper immunity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immunity is essential to make the voluntary program attractive and to permit candid communication between applicants and examiners without fear that prosecution statements will later narrow claim construction. PTO may issue regulations identifying material eligible for immunity, including materials from failed attempts, to prevent deterrence of participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTO authority to define program material and offer incentives
rubrics_metrics.description: PTO is authorized to issue regulations identifying material submitted to comply with the program that will receive file-wrapper immunity and to offer various other incentives to participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations should encourage participation by clarifying immunity scope; PTO may also run pilots and offer incentives under existing programs without new regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential costs and implementation uncertainties for applicant-quality programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical obstacles to mandating search-and-patentability requirements include unknown market for qualified private searches, uncertain costs to applicants, and the need for PTO to refine program requirements over years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These uncertainties counsel for a voluntary, incentivized trial rather than an across-the-board mandate; voluntary program data can inform future policy decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reforms to inequitable-conduct doctrine (section 11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 11 addresses reforms to the doctrine of inequitable conduct (details not fully set out in this excerpt).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reforms are intended, along with the voluntary program, to encourage applicants to be more frank with PTO and to provide information more useful to the Office.
